title: Free Hosting: Ship Your Code Without Buying Servers
subtitle: How Fly.io, Netlify and others let you deploy in seconds — and where free stops
intro: You finished a project. How do you put it on the internet without renting a whole computer?
takeaway: Free hosting lets you deploy fast on someone else's servers, but watch the limits before traffic grows.

sections.heading: Analogy: free hosting is like a free table at a food park
sections.body: Imagine you baked cookies to sell. Instead of buying a shop, a food park lets you set up a table for free. Free hosting is the same: someone else owns the computers (servers) and lets you put your site there. Deployment means copying your code onto their server so anyone can visit it.

sections.heading: Why does this exist? Ship without buying the building
sections.body:
You want to show your work fast, not manage computers. Platforms like Fly.io run your app close to users (edge deployment), and Netlify or Cloudflare Pages publish static sites straight from Git. You push to GitHub, they build and go live in seconds.

That speed is powerful. But free tables are small, and that's where it breaks.

sections.heading: What can go wrong? Free has limits
sections.body:
Free tier means a limited free allowance: maybe your site sleeps, has slow servers, or caps visitors. If 10,000 people visit at once, it can crash or charge you. JAMstack sites handle this better because they are pre-built files, not live computers.

So start free, but watch limits before you grow.

steps.narration: You push your project to GitHub.
The host detects the push and builds your site automatically.
Your site now lives on their server, not your laptop.
Edge deployment copies it close to visitors for speed.
If traffic spikes, free limits can throttle or sleep your app.

quiz.q: What does 'deployment' mean in this context?
options: Copying your code onto a host server so others can visit it
quiz.why: Deployment is putting your code on a server that serves it to the internet, like Netlify or Fly.io do.

options: To make your code run faster on your laptop
To let you showcase projects without managing servers
To hide your site from users
quiz.why: It lets developers ship and share work quickly without buying or maintaining servers.

quiz.q: What breaks first if usage grows 100x on a free tier?
options: The free allowance caps, site sleeps, slows or crashes
Edge deployment makes it 100x faster for free
quiz.why: Free tiers cap CPU, bandwidth or uptime; sudden traffic can cause sleeping, throttling or charges.

extra: Google Cloud free tier also offers limited always-free VMs for small backends.

judge.why: D2 gives the clearest beginner analogy, defines key terms in plain words, flows logically to free-tier limits, and has the strongest quiz with varied answers; its main ungrounded detail is placed in extra, though all drafts add some unsupported limit claims and exceed the word target.
